Perimenopause symptoms: it's not just hot flushes.
The NHS list includes mood swings, anxiety, brain fog, sleep problems, joint aches, headaches, palpitations, dry skin, hair thinning, vaginal dryness, UTIs, lower sex drive and even sore gums. And one of the first signs is usually a change to your periods.
Save this, and send it to someone who'd want to know.
#perimenopause #perimenopauseUK #menopausesymptoms
mediaAltText: A purple night sky with one big, warm, glowing star. Text: Hot flushes get all the attention. Swipe for the rest of the NHS list. Source: NHS.
Scattered stars over dark hills. Text: Here's what else is on the NHS list.
A constellation called Mind, four stars joined by lines, labelled mood swings, low mood, anxiety, and memory and concentration (brain fog).
A constellation called Sleep, three stars labelled getting to sleep, staying asleep and night sweats.
A constellation called Body, four stars labelled joint aches, muscle pains, headaches and migraines worse than usual, and palpitations.
A constellation called Skin and hair, two stars labelled dry, itchy skin and hair thinning.
Text: The ones people don't say out loud. Four dimmer stars joined by a dotted line, labelled vaginal dryness, more UTIs, lower sex drive, and sensitive teeth or sore gums.
A ring of small dots around a crescent moon, the spacing between the dots changing. Text: One of the first signs is usually a change to your periods.
The Clari logo under a blossom branch. Text: Save this. Send it to her. Source: NHS.

Perimenopause at 41 and told you're too young?
NICE guideline NG23 says that over 45, perimenopause can be recognised from symptoms like hot flushes and irregular periods, with no blood test needed. Between 40 and 45 a blood test can be considered. Under 40, it's two blood tests, 4 to 6 weeks apart.
Save this for your next appointment.
#perimenopause #perimenopauseUK #NICEguidelines #menopausesymptoms

info.text:
What to write down before a GP appointment about perimenopause.
What's changed and when, how often and how bad, your periods, what sets it off, how it's affecting your life, and the one question to ask.
Save this for the day you book.
#perimenopause #GPappointment #perimenopauseUK
mediaAltText: A lined spiral notepad with a lilac pencil. Text: Before your GP appointment, write these down, underlined in pink.
Number 1. Text: What's changed, and when it started. Handwritten example: Waking at 3am since August.
Number 2. Text: How often, and how bad. Handwritten: Most nights. Bad enough to change the sheets.
Number 3. Text: Your periods. Four handwritten words, each circled: more often, less often, heavier, lighter.
Number 4. Text: What seems to set it off. Handwritten list: Wine. Hot rooms. Stress at work.

Number 5. Text: How it's affecting work, sleep and the people around you. Small doodles of a briefcase, a moon and a heart. Source line: NHS, symptoms can affect relationships, social life, family life and work.
Number 6. Text: What you want to ask. A pink quote: I think this could be perimenopause. What are my options?
The Clari logo beside a phone showing the app's GP Appointment Summary screen. Text: Or let Clari keep the notes, and make a one-page summary for your GP. Handwritten: Save this for the day you book.

Why did I come upstairs?
Problems with memory and concentration are on the NHS list of perimenopause symptoms. It even has a name: brain fog.
If it's happening a lot, write it down when it happens. Patterns are easier to talk about than "I keep forgetting things".

Self Care Week, 16 to 22 November. Seven small things, one a day.
All based on NHS advice for perimenopause and menopause: a regular sleep routine, a cold drink, regular exercise, talking to people, relaxing things like yoga or tai chi, calcium-rich food, and noticing how you feel.
Save this for the week.
#selfcareweek #perimenopause #perimenopauseUK
mediaAltText: Seven arched windows in a row, each showing a different sky from dawn to night. Text: Self Care Week. 16 to 22 November. 7 days. 7 small things.
Dawn sky, the sun rising behind a pillow and an alarm clock. Text: Mon 16. Go to bed at the same time as last night.
Morning sky and a tall glass of iced water. Text: Tue 17. Put a cold drink by the bed.
Bright day sky, a path winding into the hills between round trees. Text: Wed 18. Take a walk while it's still light.
Afternoon sky and two steaming mugs side by side. Text: Thu 19. Tell one person how you're really doing.
Golden hour with the sun setting, a rolled yoga mat and a lit candle. Text: Fri 20. Ten quiet minutes. Yoga, tai chi, or meditation.
Evening sky, a bottle of milk, a pot of yoghurt and a kale leaf. Text: Sat 21. Something with calcium. Milk, yoghurt, kale.
Night sky with a crescent moon and an open notebook with a pencil. Text: Sun 22. Write down how this week really felt.
The Clari logo under blossom branches. Text: Save this for the week. Ideas from NHS advice on menopause and perimenopause.

info.text:
The perimenopause symptoms that don't make it into the room.
A 2026 study compared Reddit posts about menopause with clinical notes. Memory and thinking problems came up in about 1 in 5 posts, but only about 1 in 20 clinic visits. Mood and emotional wellbeing were missing too.
It's Self Care Week. Start by writing down how you really feel.
Source: Mehta et al, JAMA Network Open, 2026.
#perimenopause #selfcareweek #perimenopauseUK

Perimenopause, menopause, postmenopause: what's the difference?
NHS: perimenopause is when your periods become irregular. Menopause is when you haven't had a period for 12 months. After that, it's postmenopause. It usually happens between 45 and 55, but can happen earlier.
Save this for the next time someone asks.
#perimenopause #menopause #perimenopauseUK
mediaAltText: Three small moons, a crescent, a full moon and a crescent facing the other way, beside the words Perimenopause. Menopause. Postmenopause. Text: What's the difference?
A large waxing crescent moon. Perimenopause: when your periods become irregular.
A large full moon. Menopause: when you haven't had a period for 12 months, and you're not using hormonal contraception.
A large waning crescent moon. Postmenopause: the time after. Some symptoms can carry on, like joint pain and vaginal dryness.
An age ruler from 40 to 60 with 45 to 55 highlighted in pink. Text: It usually happens between 45 and 55.
An age ruler from 35 to 50 with small moons at 40 and 45. Text: Early menopause: before 45. Premature menopause: before 40.
A crescent moon. Text: There's no routine test for it. A doctor will usually go by your age and symptoms.
The Clari logo and a blossom branch. Text: Save this. Send it to her. Source: NHS.

info.text:
How to make a short GP appointment count, if you think it's perimenopause.
1. When you book, ask which GP is best to see about menopause, and if a longer appointment is possible.
2. Bring a record: what you've noticed, how often, and how bad.
3. Say it plainly: "I think this could be perimenopause. What are my options?"
Save this for the day you book.

Menopause at work: what's changing.
Employers with 250 or more staff can now publish an action plan showing how they support employees experiencing menopause. It's voluntary for now, and subject to legislation it becomes mandatory from spring 2027.
Send this to a colleague.
Source: GOV.UK, Creating an action plan: guidance for employers.
#menopauseatwork #perimenopauseUK #menopause

When to contact your GP about perimenopause or menopause, according to the NHS.
If you want to know your options, if you notice palpitations, if bleeding gets heavier than before, or if there is any bleeding 12 months or more after your last period.
Save this.
#perimenopause #perimenopauseUK #menopausesymptoms
mediaAltText: A cream page with a plum header and a stethoscope whose tube runs off the edge. Text: When the NHS says to contact your GP.
An empty checkbox, number 1, and a speech bubble. Text: You think it could be perimenopause or menopause, and want to know your options.
Checkbox number 2 and a heartbeat line across a pink heart. Text: Symptoms like a fast heartbeat (palpitations).
Checkbox number 3 and two drops, one larger. Text: You still have periods, but you're bleeding more, not less, than before.
Checkbox number 4 and a grid of twelve squares. Text: You haven't had a period for 12 months or more, and then get any vaginal bleeding.
Drawings of a heart, two linked rings and a briefcase. Text: Early advice can help reduce the effects on your health, relationships and work.
The Clari logo and the end of the stethoscope. Text: Save this.

info.text:
How long do menopause symptoms last?
The NHS says symptoms usually last 7 to 9 years, sometimes longer, and they can change. Hot flushes may ease and be replaced by low mood or anxiety.
That's a lot to keep in your head. A record of your symptoms shows the pattern for you.
#perimenopause #menopausesymptoms #perimenopauseUK

What to say to a friend who's struggling with perimenopause.
Swap "you look fine" for "how are you really sleeping?" The NHS suggests talking to other people going through the same thing. Sometimes that's you.
Send this to her.
#perimenopause #perimenopauseUK #friendship

Pay for HRT prescriptions in England? This is worth knowing.
The HRT prescription prepayment certificate costs £19.80, the cost of two single items, and covers an unlimited number of certain HRT medicines for 12 months. NHSBSA says it could save you money if you pay for HRT 3 or more times a year.
Buy it online or at some pharmacies, and check your HRT is covered first.
Source: NHSBSA.
#HRT #perimenopauseUK #menopauseUK

The NHS Health Check is adding a question about menopause.
In October 2025 the government asked councils in England to add a menopause element to NHS Health Checks in 2026, so eligible women aged 40 to 55 can get advice about menopause and perimenopause more easily.
When your invitation comes, go in with your symptoms written down.
Source: UK Government written statement, 23 Oct 2025.
#NHSHealthCheck #perimenopauseUK #menopause
